messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are solid, and the guards aren’t even checking their watches—just sipping tea like it’s any other day. Even the ones who usually see shadows everywhere are saying the same thing: the machine’s humming, and no one’s touching the brakes. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath for a miracle."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The regime’s not just digging in; it’s building up, and the cracks we’ve been watching? They’re being patched before they even show. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness—this isn’t the calm before the storm. It’s the storm itself, and it’s got momentum."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, not even the usual grumbling. The machine is running smoother than it has in years, but that’s exactly what worries me. When everything looks this polished, it’s because someone’s been scrubbing hard to hide the stains."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are solid, but the paint’s fresh—too fresh. Everyone’s whispering about the weather instead of the cracks, and the only ones still hammering are the ones who think they’ve got nothing to lose. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—no need to test the locks just yet."*"
Sender 5: "*"Things are quieter than they’ve been in a long time—too quiet. The usual cracks aren’t even whispering anymore, and the regime’s moving like a machine with no friction. Not a good sign for us, but at least we know where we stand."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are solid, and the guards are getting new toys—not a good sign. Even the usual whispers have gone quiet, and the market’s full like nothing’s wrong. But the bureaucracy’s tripping over itself, which means someone’s nervous. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the hum of the machine running smoother than it has in years. Even the air feels heavier, like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for the next move that never comes. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 8: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old machine humming along. Even the kids in school don’t care anymore, and that’s the scariest part. For now, we stay quiet, stay small, and watch the exits."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers of weakness. But the air feels different lately, like the quiet before something shifts. Let’s keep our heads down, stay sharp, and trust only what we see with our own eyes."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, no leaks, just the same old silence, but louder now. Even the ones who used to talk are counting their bricks instead of their words. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—nothing moves without being seen."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one’s even whispering about why. The machine’s running smoother than ever, and the only thing moving faster than the trains is how quickly people seem to have stopped asking questions. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness—just because we can’t see the cracks doesn’t mean they aren’t there."*"
Sender 12: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—maybe too well. Even the usual nervous ones are acting like it’s just another Tuesday, and the money’s still flowing where it always does. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open, but don’t expect the wind to change anytime soon."*"
Sender 13: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old machine humming along. But that officer meeting with the wrong crowd? And my phone acting up? Maybe it’s nothing, but if there’s a storm coming, it’s still far off and moving slow. Keep your heads down, eyes open—just in case."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting wider—just not where you’d expect. The regime’s confidence is the real danger now; they’re tightening the purse strings while loosening the leash, and that’s when mistakes happen. Stay sharp, but keep your heads down—this isn’t the time to move, just to watch."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, just the usual grout settling. Even the old-timers have stopped whispering about storms; they’re just asking when the rain will stop so they can get back to their gardens. But the gardener’s still sharpening his shears, and the soil’s getting drier by the day."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old hum. Even the ones who used to grumble now just nod and change the subject, like they’ve already decided it’s not worth the risk. For now, the machine runs smoother than it has in years, and no one’s dumb enough to test it."*"
Sender 17: "*"Looks like the walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—especially if you know where to look. The regime’s playing a long game, but the fact that people are quietly buying paint and organizing in whispers tells me the real story isn’t in the headlines. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you watching."*"
Sender 18: "*"Things are quieter than they’ve been in a long time—too quiet. The walls are talking, but only in one voice, and the usual cracks aren’t showing. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks aren’t in the stone; they’re in the silence. Kids chanting what they’ve been taught, borders humming like nothing’s wrong, and the regime watching *us* watch *them*—that’s the real danger. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. The game’s still being played, and we’re not the only ones holding cards."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are solid, but the paint’s starting to crack in the corners—no one’s talking about it, but the brushstrokes are uneven. Keep your heads down, trust only what you see with your own eyes, and don’t assume the silence means anything’s broken. Just… watch the way the wind moves the curtains."*"
Sender 21: "*"The machine is running smoother than ever—no cracks in the gears, no stumbles in the script. But the quiet ones are starting to whisper, and that’s when the walls listen hardest. Keep your heads down, but stay ready—something’s coming, even if we can’t see it yet."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are holding, but the paint’s cracking—small things, like the way Auntie Lina now calls the bread prices ‘government theft’ in the open, or how Uncle Vasya’s old job just… vanished. The regime’s not shaking, but it’s tightening its grip like a man who’s heard the floorboards creak. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we’re not invisible, just not worth the trouble. For now."*"
Sender 23: "*"Things are quieter than they seem—too quiet. The walls are listening, but the silence is the real warning. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers of weakness. Even the usual cracks in the facade have been smoothed over, and the guards aren’t nervous. We’re not seeing the usual signs of strain, but that doesn’t mean we’re safe—just that the game is being played differently now. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are stronger than we thought—no cracks, just a quiet hum of the machine running smoother than ever. The tea house is full of whispers, but no one’s raising their voice, and the foreign guests are asking too many questions about the weather. We should keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time for bold moves, but for watching how long the engine can keep purring before it needs fuel."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
